classical_baseline: The paper treats classical Monte Carlo integration, numerical PDE/ODE solvers, branch-and-bound and interior-point methods, and classical machine learning methods as the main classical baselines. For some use cases it also names specific classical approaches such as least-squares Monte Carlo, simulated annealing, and deep learning or clustering methods.
classical_baseline_quotes: One of the most widely used numerical methods is Monte Carlo integration, since it is generic and scalable to high-dimensional problems [12].
Branch-and-Bound (with cutting -planes, heuristics, etc.) for non-convex cases [26] and Interior-Point Methods for certain convex cases [27]
classical_difficulty: The paper says the classical difficulty is mainly scaling: many finance problems are high-dimensional, stochastic, and require large amounts of computation and time, while some classical methods become intractable or require exponential resources in dimension. It also notes that data loading, training, and numerical solution of PDEs can be expensive, and that some quantum advantages depend on assumptions such as sparse, well-conditioned matrices or efficient data access.
classical_difficulty_quotes: These tasks often require large amounts of computational power and time to achieve the desired precision in the solution.

We note that quantum circuits generated for gate-based quantum computers can also be simulated on classical hardware. It is generally a computationally ineﬃcient process, however, with enormous memory requirements scaling exponentially with the number of qubits [45–48].
business_stakes: The paper says the stakes include regulatory compliance, capital and risk requirements, customer retention, data security, and practical financial decision-making. It also explicitly links risk metrics to Basel III and says better efficiency and accuracy can support loan-related decisions and financial projections.
business_stakes_quotes: These regulations require computing numerous risk metrics, such as value at risk (VaR) and conditional value at risk (CVaR).
Engaging in ways to determine risk metrics with higher levels of accuracy and eﬃciency will enable ﬁnancial institutions to make better-informed loan-related decisions and ﬁnancial projections.
Financial institutions must meet this expectation in order to continue to retain their customers.
Risk modeling is also important in terms of compliance with regulations.
extraction_notes: survey paper with broad finance framing; motivation is explicit in abstract, introduction, and section 2
